messages.content:
The failing test `testLang299()` creates a new StrBuilder with initial capacity 1 and then calls appendFixedWidthPadRight("foo", 1, '-').

The current bug report points out a bug in StrBuilder.appendFixedWidthPadRight(Object, int, char), specifically highlighting that the code calls str.getChars(0, strLen, buffer, size) when strLen >= width, but this is wrong and causes an ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException.

Looking at the method appendFixedWidthPadRight:

- If width > 0, ensureCapacity(size + width) is called to make sure buffer can hold the new content.

- Then the string representation of obj is obtained (or getNullText() if null).

- Then strLen is computed.

- If strLen >= width, str.getChars is called with arguments (0, strLen, buffer, size).

- Else, if strLen < width, str.getChars is called with the same arguments (0, strLen, buffer, size) followed by padding characters added from buffer[size + strLen] to buffer[size + width -1].

- Finally size is incremented by width.

The bug happens in the first branch when strLen >= width: the method should only write 'width' characters from str into buffer starting at position size, but the code calls str.getChars(0, strLen, buffer, size) which tries to write strLen characters.

Since the buffer length is only ensured to handle 'size + width' characters by ensureCapacity, attempting to write strLen characters starting at position size will cause an ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException if strLen > width.

Similarly, in the padding branch, calling str.getChars with strLen seems safe since strLen < width, and buffer has capacity for size + width, so no overflow should occur.

This matches the description in the bug report that the line

    str.getChars(0, strLen, buffer, size);

should instead be

    str.getChars(0, width, buffer, size);

to only copy 'width' characters in the case strLen >= width.

In the failing test, "foo" length is 3, width is 1, so strLen >= width is true.

The faulty code tries to write 3 characters starting at buffer position size, but buffer only has space for 1 character (size + width), leading to ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException.

Therefore, the root cause is that in appendFixedWidthPadRight, when strLen >= width, it copies too many characters from str into buffer overflowing it.

# Diagnosis

The bug in StrBuilder.appendFixedWidthPadRight causes an ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException in tests where the input string length is greater than the width parameter. This occurs because the method copies 'strLen' characters (the full length of the string) into the buffer starting at position 'size', but only ensures the buffer capacity to hold 'size + width' characters. When strLen > width, this leads to an out-of-bounds write in the buffer array. The fix is to limit the number of characters copied from str to 'width' when strLen >= width. The rest of the method logic is correct because it pads the remaining width if strLen < width. The failing test demonstrates this issue by requesting to append "foo" with width 1, causing overflow.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
